# Lesson Plan: "Reading for Real Life" — Signs, Forms & Instructions

**Duration:** 90 minutes | **Group size:** Designed to flex from 4–14 learners | **Level:** Mixed ability, Entry 1–3 equivalent

---

## Why this design

Because attendance is unpredictable and motivations vary widely, this plan avoids sequencing that depends on "what we did last time." Instead, it uses a **self-contained theme with tiered, self-selecting stations**, so every learner — whether it's their first session or their tenth — can join at their own level and work toward their own goal (parenting, driving, employment, independence).

---

## Learning Outcomes (broad enough to suit all learners)

By the end of the session, learners will be able to:
- Locate specific information in a short, real-life text
- Follow a short sequence of written instructions
- Recognise and use key vocabulary in context

---

## Preparation Checklist (do once, reuse indefinitely)

Build a **reusable resource box** with laminated real-world texts, organised into three tiers by colour (green = emerging reader, amber = developing, blue = confident). Include at least one item relevant to each common learner goal:

| Theme | Example texts |
|---|---|
| Driving | Road sign chart, highway code excerpt, parking notice, insurance renewal letter |
| Parenting/school | School newsletter, homework instruction sheet, permission slip, reading record |
| Daily life/work | Medicine label, bus timetable, job application form, payslip |

For each text, prepare a **task card** (3 tiers) with 3–5 simple questions, and a **self-check answer card** so learners can verify their own work without waiting for a tutor.

Other materials:
- Sign-in sheet (doubles as name/date writing practice)
- "Skills Passport" folders — one per learner, kept at the venue, updated every session regardless of attendance gaps
- Stickers/stamps for logging progress
- Whiteboard/flipchart, pens, highlighters

---

## Room Setup

Arrange 3–5 themed stations (driving / school-home / daily life-work / forms / mixed) around the room. Each station holds tiered materials for that theme. This setup works whether you have one learner per table or four.

---

## Timed Agenda

| Time | Activity | Notes on flexibility |
|---|---|---|
| **0–10 min** | **Arrival & sign-in.** Learners write name/date on sign-in sheet (tutor assists as needed). Informal chat; hand out/retrieve Skills Passports. | Self-paced — works if people trickle in. No content missed if someone arrives late. |
| **10–20 min** | **Whole-group hook.** Show 2–3 real texts (a road sign, a school note, a medicine label). Ask: "Where might you see this? What do you need to know from it?" Brief discussion. | Doesn't require prior knowledge; works with 4 or 14 people as open discussion. |
| **20–30 min** | **Modelled strategy (whole group).** Tutor demonstrates one simple strategy — e.g., "scan for the key word first" — using one shared text on the whiteboard. Think-aloud style. | Keep short and concrete; this is the only "taught" input, so it must stand alone. |
| **30–65 min** | **Station work (differentiated, self-selected).** Learners choose a station matching their goal/interest and pick a tiered task card matching their comfort level. Work alone, in pairs, or small groups. Tutor(s)/volunteers circulate. Learners may rotate once if time allows. | Scales naturally: small group = 1:1 tutoring feel; large group = peer support, buddy pairing of returners with newcomers. |
| **65–80 min** | **Goal-focused application.** Learners apply the skill to something personally relevant: a driving theory practice question, a real school letter, or a form they've brought in. Tutor supports individually. | Fully individualised — no dependency on group progress. |
| **80–88 min** | **Whole-group share-back.** 2–3 volunteers briefly say one thing they read/learned today. Tutor highlights common vocabulary or strategies across different stations. | Works with any number; keep brief if group is large. |
| **88–90 min** | **Close & takeaway.** Stamp Skills Passports. Offer an optional take-home slip (same text, one more question) for those who want it — no pressure, no penalty if not returned. | Ends cleanly; nothing is "owed" for next week. |

---

## Differentiation Strategies

- **Tiered materials, not tiered groups** — learners self-select difficulty, preserving dignity.
- **Buddy system** — pair experienced attendees with newcomers at stations; builds community and reduces tutor load in larger groups.
- **Multiple modalities** — visual (signs/icons), oral (reading aloud optional), written (task cards) so no one is excluded by starting level.
- **Self-check answer cards** reduce bottlenecks when only one tutor is present with 14 learners.

---

## Handling Irregular Attendance

- **No cumulative content** — each session is a complete unit in itself.
- **Skills Passport** stored at the venue tracks individual progress across sporadic attendance without requiring learners to "catch up."
- **Flexible entry point** — learners can join mid-session (e.g., arriving 20 minutes late still lands them at a station doing meaningful work).

## Handling Variable Numbers

- **4 learners:** Run as one-to-one/pair tutoring at 2–3 stations; skip rotation; extend application time.
- **14 learners:** Use all stations plus any volunteer helpers; rely more on buddy pairing and self-check cards; whole-group segments stay tightly timed to preserve individual work time.

---

## Assessment (informal, ongoing)

No tests. Tutor uses a simple observation checklist during station work (can learner locate information? follow a sequence? identify key words?) and logs brief notes in each learner's Skills Passport — useful for continuity even when attendance is inconsistent.
